drafted_from: tool:publish-a-list-view-as-a-file row (tools/export-records-as-list-rows/tool-rows.json), do-work/publish_view_file.py, read-data/view_publish.py and test/test_view_publish.py; the answers are what the script printed on made-up bakery news rows
start_here: Say to your AI: "Publish what my news view shows into site/news.json so my website can render it, and tell me whether the file changed."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it takes one read of a saved view from a file and writes the rows into one file for a site.
instructions: 1. Read the saved view with tool:read-a-list-view into read.json, with a limit at least the number of rows the view shows, so the read holds the whole view.
2. Write pub-config.json with view set to the saved view's record id (add media only when its pictures must be copied into the site).
3. Say "Publish my view as a file"; your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs its command from the Workshop checkout with {read}, {config} and {out}.
4. Read rows of of, and written: true means the file changed, false means it already held these rows. Deploy the site yourself when you agree.

worked_examples.title: Two of four news rows are published, then nothing changes
worked_examples.ask: Publish what my news view shows into site/news.json.
worked_examples.given: Read from a real run of do-work/publish_view_file.py (the same shape test/test_view_publish.py uses). The AI runs: python3 -I tools/export-records-as-list-rows/do-work/publish_view_file.py --read read.json --config pub-config.json --out site/news.json. read.json is a complete read of list news (of 4) holding row tarts (title Lemon tarts, stage Out, day 2026-03-09) and row rye (title Rye on Sundays, stage Out, day 2026-02-01); pub-config.json is {"view":"list-view:news:shown"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: First run: {"file": "site/news.json", "rows": 2, "of": 4, "blake3": "aac18c407c8082202035abbce62455c1c05419b94d624b20b31d7988db41492a", "media": {"copied": 0, "kept": 0, "not_public": 0}, "written": true}. The same command again prints the same blake3 with "written": false and leaves the file untouched. site/news.json holds schema list-view-file/v1, source {view, list: news, blake3}, the four fields and the two rows in order.
